articles.title: 5 Deadly Demons From Hell Who Could Become a Threat to Doctor Doom's Throne
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Doctor Doom shockingly became the ruler of Hell after his death, and there are several other demons that he needs to beware of. This event happened in the pages of Captain America, when Steve Rogers ended up in a coma, and Doom called his soul to Hell to help him overthrow Mephisto. What Rogers didn't […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Doctor Doom shockingly became the ruler of Hell after his death, and there are several other demons that he needs to beware of. This event happened in the pages of Captain America, when Steve Rogers ended up in a coma, and Doom called his soul to Hell to help him overthrow Mephisto. What Rogers didn't know was that Doom would take the position for himself, free everyone from their contracts, and allow anyone who wanted to leave to do so. This caused several problems, which play out in the new Avengers series, where the broken deals have come due, and in the Black Panther & Namor Doomed , where someone is trying to overthrow Doom in Hell. This should come as no surprise since it is obvious demons would not be happy with Doom calling himself their ruler.

In fact, there are several demons who would probably love to step into Doctor Doom's role, and many of them are more qualified to rule in a demonic realm than Victor von Doom. While some of these demons might already have designs to challenge Doom, others might be sitting just outside of his realm, preparing to strike when the time is right.

S'ym debuted in Uncanny X-Men #160 (1982) by Chris Claremont and Brent Anderson. In that issue, the X-Men chase Illyana Rasputin into Limbo, the realm ruled by Belasco. S'ym is one of the threats Belasco's domain throws at them, and he proves to be a bigger danger than anyone could have expected. He is one of the strongest demons in Limbo, and he was powerful enough to even defeat Colossus when the two battled hand-to-hand. However, his true might was shown during the "Inferno" event when Madelyne Pryor tried to bring Hell to Earth.

Before this event, he was infected by a techno-organic virus, which lets him re-form from a single molecule. Illyana's Soulsword, once one of the few weapons that could kill him, stopped working on his new circuitry body. He and fellow demon N'astirh took in Madelyne Pryor as part of a demonic invasion of Earth that was set to start with Manhattan. In the recent X-Orcists series, Madelyne Pryor and Magik have to team up because an uprising is brewing in Limbo, and someone like S'ym could be a threat to Doctor Doom, especially since he has served as the ruler of Limbo.

Satannish made his first appearance in Doctor Strange #174 (1968) by Roy Thomas and Gene Colan. His origin showed his powers. Lord Nekron spent a year drawing occult power from Satannish on the condition that he deliver an equally skilled mystic as Satannish's slave. Nekron picked Doctor Strange, lost, and Satannish took Nekron's soul instead. His origin makes him a direct rival to anyone holding Hell. He also has ties to one of the most powerful supernatural characters in Marvel Comics.

Dormammu created Satannish and placed him among the Hell Lords as an undercover agent, and Satannish rules his own dimension next to Earth. He even has a cult, the Sons of Satannish, and at one time, they used the Book of the Vishanti to summon Surtur and Ymir, a story that crossed from Doctor Strange comics into Avengers comics. His mystic power is virtually unlimited, and it has been shown to equal Mephisto's. As a demon who equals Mephisto in power and already runs his own hell, he has an obvious motive to grab the bigger throne while the new ruler is settling in.

Belasco was the ruler of Limbo and one of the most powerful demons in existence. Belasco debuted in Ka-Zar the Savage #11 (1981) by Bruce Jones and Brent Anderson. His origin story ties him to Dante. Belasco was a 13th-century Italian sorcerer who kidnapped Beatrice Portinari, Dante's beloved, and Dante attacked him after Beatrice died in childbirth. Belasco then made a pact with the Elder Gods of the N'Garai, who gave him immortality and power in exchange for helping them cross into Earth's dimension using five Bloodstones.

Ka-Zar destroyed his locket, which trapped Belasco in Limbo for years. He then conquered it. His most important moment in Marvel history was when he turned a child, Illyana Rasputin, into his apprentice and shaped part of her soul into a Bloodstone, until she rebelled, drove him out, and became Magik. His grip on Limbo slipped, and Mary Jane Watson and the Black Cat defeated him, giving his Soulsword to S'ym, who became the new ruler. Belasco is one of the most powerful sorcerers in Marvel Comics, and after losing his realm, there is no reason to think that he won't come after Doctor Doom's throne.

There is more than one Lilith in Marvel Comics, and one of the most famous is Dracula's daughter. However, this Lilith is the original mythical character, the Mother of Demons. She debuted in Ghost Rider #28 (1992) by Howard Mackie and Andy Kubert. The issue also introduced her son Meatmarket and the Caretaker, and it was the start of the 1992 crossover series, "Rise of the Midnight Sons." In fact, it was Lilith who coined the name Midnight Sons at the end of that series.

In her origin, she is an immortal demon goddess and sorceress who survived pre-Cataclysm Atlantis. Atlantean sorcerers trapped her inside the leviathan Tiamat, and over the centuries she gave birth to the Lilin, a family that includes Blackout, Creed, Pilgrim, and Nakota. She can create new Lilin, rebirth fallen children, and even rebirth herself into a younger body, which makes her hard to remove for good. Doctor Doom inherited a Hell full of demons, and Lilith is literally the mother of a demon bloodline. A ruler who can raise an army of her own children and resurrect herself does not need Doom's permission to stay in power.

Out of all the demons who might want to overthrow Doctor Doom, Mephisto sits at the top of the list. This is because it was his realm, and Doctor Doom won the throne through trickery. Mephisto is already planning his return, as he has shown up on Earth. This was in The Avengers #1 (2026), during the moments when Doom's decree that ended all of Mephisto's deals led to an onslaught of murderous angels descending on society. Mephisto has shown in that first issue that he is planning something, likely a means to regain his throne.

Mephisto debuted in Silver Surfer #3 (1968) by Stan Lee and John Buscema. Lee and Buscema based him on Mephistopheles, the tempter from the Faust legend, and he has symbolized the devil in many of his Marvel Comics storylines. His feud with Doctor Doom is personal. In Doctor Strange & Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment (1989) by Roger Stern and Mike Mignola, Doom beat him to win the freedom of his mother's soul. Doom beat him again in the Captain America series, and Mephisto will never take defeat lying down.

What are your thoughts on Doctor Doom taking control of Hell? Let us know who you think could bring Doom down in the comments below.

articles.summary: It should come as no surprise to anyone that Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is absolutely killing it at the box office during its opening weekend. But the long-awaited Haymitch Abernathy-centered prequel is doing even better than some expected, bringing in what looks like an estimated 70% of all box office cash on its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It should come as no surprise to anyone that Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is absolutely killing it at the box office during its opening weekend. But the long-awaited Haymitch Abernathy-centered prequel is doing even better than some expected, bringing in what looks like an estimated 70% of all box office cash on its $56 million opening day. This puts the movie on track for an insane $120 million-plus opening weekend—but it also guarantees it another honor: dethroning Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey for the third-biggest opening day of 2026.

This incredible opening weekend also marks Lionsgate Studio's first time clearing a $100 million opening weekend since The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part II released in 2015 ( Mockingjay Part I opened to $121 million on its opening weekend in 2014). And these aren't the only accolades Sunrise on the Reaping has earned—it also has an A- Cinemascore and an impressive 95% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics, however, are less impressed . But die-hard fans of the franchise, as well as first-time viewers, are along for the ride as the layers of this fan-favorite character are peeled back in graphic, heartbreaking detail .

While critics feel that Haymitch's story merely retreads old ground, fans disagree, claiming that it adds more depth to an already deep, dark story. "Sturdy and well-made—director Francis Lawrence has now made five of these and certainly knows what he's doing—but at this point, it's clear these movies are continuing because they're still box office draws, not because there's more story to tell," says critic Brett Arnold . Though critic Abhimanyu Mathur says, "If a Hunger Games film is never made again, this may just be the most satisfying and perfect way to end this saga."

And if the sheer number of ticket sales didn't speak to how casual viewers feel about the continuation of the Hunger Games saga, their reviews and the aforementioned A-CinemaScore certainly do. One viewer said, "Phenomenal movie all around! Joseph Zada kills it as Haymitch as well as amazing performances from the whole cast. This is up there at the top with Catching Fire for me." Another summed up the audience's views perfectly, saying, " Sunrise on the Reaping does a fantastic job balancing nostalgia and familiarity with something new, giving Haymitch’s story the depth it deserves. The casting couldn't have been better, with everyone convincingly playing younger versions of our characters without coming across as imitations."

While critics and audiences are divided, as is often the case, it seems that the ticket sales are speaking for themselves, and Sunrise on the Reaping will at least go down in history as the film that took down The Odyssey at the theater (and snagged another $100+ million opening weekend for Lionsgate).

Of course, this past week there was some big news on the front, as it was finally confirmed that Robert Pattinson would play the new 007 . All the while, many are still wondering who will be the next Bond Girl. My pick is Alexandra Daddario , and I'm not the only one who feels that way. Now, amid the rumors, Daddario is weighing in.

According to recent reports that have dropped, the race for the position of next Bond Girl is becoming quite interesting. So far, prediction market Kalshi’s got Margaret Qualley topping Sydney Sweeney for its pick, followed by names like Anya Taylor-Joy and Florence Pugh along with others. While Daddario’s not on that list, it's no surprise she's still been linked to Bond 26 speculation. While speaking to Hollywood ReelTime , the fan-favorite actress shared a level-headed take:

The internet says things. I don’t really know. (laughs) I mean, I’m very excited to see the Bond movie, but I don’t believe I’ll be in it. I don’t know. The internet can say anything, I guess.

Based on the Couples Weekend star's laughter throughout her response, I’m curious if she knows something we don’t. But, like her Hershey costar Finn Witrock said, “Never say never.” I personally think Daddario would do a great job, as she has more than enough charm to pull it off. When looking back at the most iconic Bond Girls throughout history , they've each had elements of seen glamour, intelligence, emotional depth and mystery, and Daddario can embody all of those attributes.

We clearly know the Mayfair Witches actress has the beauty that’ll surely make the MI6 agent swoon. Whether she's wowing us with an end-of-summer bikini or giving Hollywood glamour in a gorgeous backless dress , fashionista Daddario would be perfect for it. Not to mention, any Bond can fall under the spell of her piercing blue eyes .

Other than looking like a true beauty, though, the Texas Chainsaw 3D star has experience with action movies like the Percy Jackson films and San Andreas . Daddario has also played characters who are vulnerable and emotionally guarded. Through her award-recognized portrayal of Rachel in The White Lotus , she played a woman experiencing internal struggles and conflicting emotions about her husband.

Now That We Know Who Is Playing James Bond, Who Could Be The Next Bond Girl? I’m Glad People Are Out There Asking Rumored Bond Girls How They'd Feel About Joining Robert Pattinson The New James Bond Is Finally Confirmed, And I’m Shocked Also, in True Detective , Daddario's character, Lisa, refuses to be disregarded while serving as a mistress to Detective Hart. So, with these two HBO roles alone, I believe Daddario can give both sensuality and substance while playing a Bond Girl. I also want to see her chemistry with Robert Pattinson . While the two have never done a project together, I can see them playing off each other well.

While we don’t know yet who will be the lucky lady to play the next Bond Girl, I'm keeping my fingers crossed for Alexandra Daddario to get the part. Hopefully, additional information on the upcoming film -- which is being directed by Denis Villeneuve -- will arrive sooner rather than later. In the meantime, though, you can watch Daddario in the 2026 movie release Hershey , which is in theaters now.

“Sunrise on the Reaping” generated $56 million from 4,018 North American theaters on Friday, taking the No. 1 spot. Joseph Zada, McKenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning and more star, with appearances from original “The Hunger Games” cast members Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woodey Harleson.

articles.summary: Courtesy of Shueisha Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has officially brought the end to the long running anime after 22 years, and a new look has been revealed at a huge event coming next year to help say goodbye to the franchise after all this time. Tite Kubo's Bleach initially made its return to screens with a new adaptation […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has officially brought the end to the long running anime after 22 years, and a new look has been revealed at a huge event coming next year to help say goodbye to the franchise after all this time. Tite Kubo's Bleach initially made its return to screens with a new adaptation of the long awaited final arc of the manga a few years ago, and after four seasons, this new era of the anime has indeed come to an end. But fans are getting one last chance to say goodbye .

Bleach Fes. has been announced as a major new event coming to Japan over the February 27-28 weekend, and it's going to feature members of the production staff and voice cast as they look back on two decades of the anime and say their goodbyes. While there are no potential international plans revealed for the anime as of this time, a new poster has been revealed giving a cool look at the anime's characters ahead of the event's debut. Check it out below.

It's yet to be detailed what kind of event that Bleach Fes. will ultimately turn out to be, but it's meant to be a celebration of how far the anime has come over its 22 year run as those behind the scenes look back on their time with the project. But while the TV anime series has come to an end, there are still many questions lingering about the potential future of the franchise. Because as fans know well enough by now, t here actually is more in store for Bleach' s original manga story .

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its final episode with a time skip reintroducing Ichigo Kurosaki and the others ten years after the fight against Yhwach, and gave fans the first look at Ichigo and Orihime's son, Kazui. This was meant to originally be a fun button on the final moments of the series, but decades later Kubo actually returned to the story with a new one-shot that actually picked up after the original end of the series. In fact, Kubo started a whole new arc.

Bleach "No Breathes From Hell" was an official one-shot story that saw Kubo return to Shonen Jump to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the manga's original debut a few years back. That's also where this new iteration of the anime was first announced to be in production, and thus is kicked off a whole new wave of returns for the franchise. But what makes this new one-shot interesting was the fact that it introduced an entirely new realm with new, but familiar enemies to face off against .

Set after the events of Bleach' s original manga finale, this new one-shot introduced Hell to the series and revealed that many of the fallen foes (and potentially former allies) had been imprisoned in the mysterious region and changed as a result. But with no plans to continue the manga or anime as of this time, it's left as a big cliffhanger. Do you want to see Bleach' s anime return for the Hell Arc someday? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Batman #1 Is One of the Most Iconic Comic Books Ever Published, But Its Cover Left Out Two Legendary Debuts
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Whether it's Zatanna and the "Machine that Magnetized Men" or Wonder Woman in All-Star Comics #8, there is no funnier recurring phenomenon in the world of comic book collecting than major characters debuting in comics that don't bother to mention them on the cover. 1940's Batman #1 is no exception, because as classic as Jerry […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Whether it's Zatanna and the "Machine that Magnetized Men" or Wonder Woman in All-Star Comics #8 , there is no funnier recurring phenomenon in the world of comic book collecting than major characters debuting in comics that don't bother to mention them on the cover. 1940's Batman #1 is no exception, because as classic as Jerry Robinson's cover is, it manages to miss the issue's greatest selling point: the first appearances of the Joker and Catwoman, two of the most iconic characters in comic book history. That doesn't have any effect on the comic's value, however, as even this low-grade 3.0 CGC (Certified Guarantee Company)-graded copy has already attained a $140k price at auction through Heritage. Parodied, homaged, and referenced countless times through the decades, Batman #1 is still one of the most recognizable images of the Caped Crusader ever drawn; and one of the absolute most important comics DC ever published — even putting aside the iconic pair of characters who debuted within.

Although rebooted three times and no longer retaining its original numbering, the title is still running — and this month's issue even featured the Joker, introduced eighty-six years and nine hundred-odd issues ago. There are a literal handful of books able to claim such a lineage, especially taking into account that Batman has published continuously for those eighty-six years, a testament to the character's enduring popularity. At the time, he was one of just two DC heroes given multiple monthly titles, the other being Superman . Virtually every major change and trend in the comic book medium can be traced through those eighty-six years of Batman stories, which would introduce readers to iconic characters like Ra's al Ghul and Poison Ivy, as well as stories better left in the past, like the time Batman and Robin tried to solve the "Paul is Dead" mystery .

Batman #1 opens with "The Legend of the Batman - Who He is, and How He Came to Be," a reprint from Detective Comics #33. In two pages, it provides the backstory that has come to be completely engrained in popular culture, establishing the murder of Thomas and Martha Wayne in a dark Gotham alley while returning from the movies with their son Bruce. From this origin reprint, the issue launches in its first new story, entitled simply "The Joker." Here we meet the Ace of Knaves as a violent, cunning maniac; an arrogant killer who announces his crimes before he commits them, confident he will not be stopped. Each of his victims is left with a grotesque smile on their faces, the result of a deadly dose of "Joker venom." After besting the Dynamic Duo several times, the Joker makes the fatal mistake of mentioning his next target in earshot of a captive Robin, enabling the escaped Robin and Batman to foil the robbery in-progress. The Joker is sent to prison, vowing revenge on his newfound nemesis — revenge that would come later that same issue.

"The Joker's Revenge" once again sees him outwit Batman continuously, and cements what makes him the Dark Knight's greatest foe: his madness. Unstable and erratic, the Joker's wanton violence and unpredictable derangement lend him an edge on Batman's regimented, logical thinking. In this issue, the Joker kills without pattern, leaves behind the target of a successful robbery, and fakes his own death. After the fake-out, Gotham Police (and readers) learn that the Joker is still alive, indicating that writer Bill Finger knew what he had with the character, and was planning his next move already. It would come in "The Case of the Laughing Death" in Detective Comics #45, followed by a team-up with Catwoman in Batman #2. That issue would also mark the first time the name "Catwoman" was used, as for her first appearance, Selina Kyle's alter ego is "the Cat."

Like the Joker, Catwoman emerges pretty fully formed, name non-withstanding. The story is actually a spotlight for Robin, who goes undercover on a Gotham socialite's yacht after correctly deducing her emerald necklace (worth $500,000 — and that's in 1940) will prove too tempting a target for the city's criminal element. Robin's hunch proves correct, and the thief in question is "the Cat," herself a member of Gotham's upper crust and a passenger aboard the yacht. Though the theft is foiled and she is discovered as the Cat by Batman at the story's end, Selina Kyle is able to escape from justice. How? Batman is taken in by her beauty, and momentarily stunned by her offer to switch sides and join her as the "King of Crime." She dives overboard from the yacht, and Batman lets her go, marking the beginning of one of the most iconic, tumultuous romances in comic books.

The issue is rounded out by a Hugo Strange story, rooting it firmly in its era. Prior to the debut of the Joker, Hugo Strange was the defacto nemesis of Batman as his first recurring opponent. As the decade continued, Hugo Strange would be overshadowed by other members of Batman's growing rogues gallery, returning to prominence decades later following a revival in Steve Englehart's justly-renowned Detective Comics run. Pitting Batman against Hugo Strange's mutated "Monster Men," this story provides what may actually be the issue's most-discussed moment: Batman kills. In a struggle with one of the Monster Men, the mutant is left hanging from the Bat-Plane's rope, implicitly fatally, based on a comment that he is "better off this way" from Batman. His "no killing" rule would be codified three issues later in Batman #4, further positioning Batman #1 at a major crossroads in the history of the character.

Although this is difficult to fathom today, Batman was in serious danger of cancellation in the early sixties. Neutered by the Comics Code Authority, DC's writers and artists were forced to avoid Batman's rogues' gallery, who were considered inappropriate to younger readers. The Joker and Catwoman were singled out in particular, with the Joker's gleeful violence and Catwoman's sexually-charged dynamic with Batman seen as bad influences. While Joker was toned down to emphasize his pranks and downplay his homicidal tendencies, Catwoman disappeared altogether. It would take the 1966 Batman television series to revive the character, who quickly became one of its most popular recurring villains. Played by Julie Newmar, Catwoman was one of four Batman villains to appear in the feature adaptation of the series, 1966's Batman: The Movie . After a more than decade-long absence, Catwoman returned to comics in Superman's Girl Friend, Lois Lane #70. The television series' popularity also forced editor Julius Schwartz to continue using the Joker in Batman stories despite his personal distaste for the character.

The boost in Batman readership proved temporary, and DC's response to the title's next dip in sales proved even more consequential: a return to Batman's darker roots, ushered in by creators like Denny O'Neil, Neal Adams, and Jim Aparo. While no longer an influence over the tone of the comics, the Batman television series left its permanent mark on who were considered central to the character's mythology and rogues' gallery. The Joker would be one of the first to benefit from the new direction, returning to his terrifying homicidal maniac roots in Batman #251, "The Joker's Five-Way Revenge." Catwoman evolved throughout the 1970s and 80s, with her alternate universe Earth-Two counterpart leaving behind her life of crime and marrying Bruce Wayne — suggesting that maybe the primary, Earth-One Selena Kyle could do the same. Len Wein's Batman work played with Catwoman's reform, turning her into an anti-hero, a characterization that has stuck in the decades since.

Tim Burton's Batman and Batman Returns further cemented the Joker and Catwoman's place in popular culture, as have the litany of further live-action and animated adaptations that have come in the intervening decades. Even in Batman #1, it's apparent why creators find themselves returning to the characters again and again: both provide excellent foils to Batman, challenging him in ways that speak to his beliefs, ethics, and what makes him a super-hero. Put into the context of a retelling of his origin, and the last time he ever killed without hesitation or regret, the Joker and Catwoman's relationships with Batman become even more complex — and Batman #1 even more significant. And with just three hundred and fifty-six copies on the CGC's population report, the record-setting prices that the issue can sell for are no surprise. With its rarity and significance taken into account, the copy on auction at Heritage starts to look like a bargain, even for $100k.

articles.title: Lindsay Hubbard Teases 'Summer House' Spinoff 'In the City' Season 2: "Better Than Season One"
articles.summary: The reality star also addresses reports of a recent kiss with Bravo co-star Kyle Cooke, opens up about motherhood, her partnership with No Kid Hungry and upcoming memoir, 'Activated.'
articles.content:
Amid filming season two of Bravo 's In the City , being a mom and her charitable efforts, Lindsay Hubbard is having a busy fall.

Hubbard's latest venture is partnering with No Kid Hungry's Amplify Impact campaign ahead of Thanksgiving. The reality star served free breakfast sandwiches to New Yorkers at Give Back Bodega alongside season 21 Top Chef winner Danny Garcia at a pop-up event in Manhattan earlier this week. The campaign aims to help 10 million more kids access meals by 2032.

"One in five kids faces hunger every day in the United States, and as a kid, they should just be kids. They should be playing and having a good time, and they shouldn't have to think about where their next meal is coming from," she told The Hollywood Reporter . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up Movies 'I Play Rocky' Stars Unite With Original 'Rocky' Producer for Film's 50th Anniversary Celebration

The cause has taken on an even greater significance for Hubbard as a mother. Her daughter, Gemma Britt Kufe, turns two next month, and she explained how motherhood has changed her perspective on childhood hunger.

"When I'm with Gemma, I have no nannies. I'm single mom-ing it hard," she said. "I am spending my days feeding her, caring for her, making sure she's eating. That's the one thing that I'm always constantly thinking about. Even me growing up, I didn't have to worry about where my next meal is coming from, so of course my perspective changes because it's sad that we live in a world where one in five kids doesn't have meals."

While she remained tight-lipped about the upcoming season because the show is currently in production, she teased that fans will be satisfied with what's to come.

"We're in the middle of filming it right now, and let me tell you, it's got all of the elements of a great season two, better than season one," Hubbard said.

Page Six reported in October that the sophomore season will feature a cast shake-up. According to the outlet, new castmembers include Brittany Whitfield, Robert Morrison, Reagan Baker, Natasha Parker and Barthelemy Jallet. Meanwhile, season one stars Amanda Batula, Danielle Olivera and her partner, Eoin Heavey, as well as Andrea Denver and his wife, Lexi Sundin, will not be returning.

Batula's departure comes amid a particularly eventful period for the Summer House cast. Batula and her husband, OG Summer House star Kyle Cooke , had separated before the reports surfaced. Cooke was also close friends with Wilson. In alleged Instagram DMs, Batula cited intense online "hate" and "bullying" over her relationship with Wilson as her reason for not returning. Bravo has yet to officially announce the cast for In the City season two and did not respond to THR's request for comment.

Meanwhile, Hubbard herself has made headlines amid filming for the upcoming season. Earlier this month, Page Six reported that Cooke made out with Hubbard over Halloween weekend while filming a cast trip in Cancun, Mexico. Hubbard addressed the speculation with a laugh, telling THR, "No, Kyle's like a brother to me. We just have a lot of fun, you know.”

"I'll do it as long as they'll have me on all these shows. I live a really big, full life that rarely ever stops. Things happen, and I have a lot to share at all times," she said. "So until that stops, then maybe the TV portion would stop for me, but I don't see that stopping anytime soon."

Also forthcoming is Hubbard's memoir, Activated , which will be released May 18. Despite spending a decade on television, she said she still has plenty of stories she hasn't shared with audiences.

"I don't need to rehash things that you can go back and rewatch," she said of what readers can expect from the book. "So it's all the stories that happen in life. articles.title: GTA 6 Players Warned Not to Make Major Chapter 1 Mistake
articles.summary: GTA 6 players have been warned by fellow Grand Theft Auto VI players, further into the new Rockstar Games release, not to make a major Chapter 1 mistake as they did. Obviously, spoilers for GTA 6's first chapter are ahead, including how the chapter finishes. That said, without knowing the spoiler, there is no way […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google GTA 6 players have been warned by fellow Grand Theft Auto VI players, further into the new Rockstar Games release, not to make a major Chapter 1 mistake as they did. Obviously, spoilers for GTA 6's first chapter are ahead, including how the chapter finishes. That said, without knowing the spoiler, there is no way to avoid the mistake, as it's not something you would predict would be a problem.

Over on the GTA 6 Reddit page, one of the top recent posts is titled, "Something you should know about the end of Chapter 1 to save you from disappointment." The warning is simply: be careful with how you spend your money in the first chapter. One of the first instincts when starting a new Grand Theft Auto is to grind in order to get your money up. That said, at the end of the first game's chapter, you will lose all your money and you lose Jason's car. To this end, there's no point boosting your bank account or upgrading Jason's car throughout the first chapter because it won't carry over to the second chapter. It's a bit of a gut punch, in fact.

What does carry over are your weapons and cosmetic items like clothing and tattoos. So, feel free to dump as much money into this as you'd like. You can also put 5,000 into the family saver, as this also won't be lost like the money in your bank account.

As you would expect, GTA 6 fans aren't huge fans of this surprise, as it greatly undermines the time of players in favor of nothing that really enhances the experience of the game.

"Yeah, I was infuriated when I had put $5k into Jason's El Camino and another $10k in the bank, only for the game to go WHOOPS, ALL GONE," reads the top comment on the post. "I don't even know if I want to do any side activities until I know the game is done tutorializing and is actually fully opened up."

Another comment adds, "Glad I rolled the dice and read this. I get put off easily by shit like this. Thank you, I would have tricked out the car and saved money for days."

Unfortunately, there are quite a few ways that GTA 6 greatly undermines the time of players, whether it's in favor of arbitrary immersion, an obsession with realism, or for the progression of the narrative. In isolation, none of it is that consequential, but in totality, it can feel limiting, tedious, and frustrating. This, among other reasons, may be why it has a low user review score on Metacritic . That said, Rockstar Games won't care very much, considering GTA 6 is the biggest launch in entertainment history by raw numbers, and it's not even close.

Grand Theft Auto VI is available via PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S, and Xbox Series X. Those interested in playing it at launch will need to fork over a minimum of $80.

It's been an eventful year for the My Hero Academia franchise as with it celebrating its 10th anniversary, the anime has been making a comeback with all sorts of new projects and events . There's been no better time to be a fan of the anime, and now that's even more true thanks to one of its formerly missing movies finally being available.

Crunchyroll has now officially launched My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission with the streaming platform , and it's now available to watch after five long years. Originally hitting theaters in Japan, available for purchase on Blu-ray and digital platforms , and streaming with other platforms such as Netflix, the fourth film in the anime franchise has now come to Crunchyroll so fans can check it out all over again.

My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission is now streaming with Crunchyroll in both Japanese and English language audio with availability depending on region. Serving as the fourth entry in the My Hero Academia feature film franchise , this one is directed by Kenji Nagasaki for studio Bones and TOHO Animation with a script provided by Yosuke Kuroda, character designs provided by Yoshihiko Umakoshi, and music composed by Yuki Hayashi. Originally releasing back in 2021, it's been a long time coming for this streaming release with Crunchyroll.

My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission took Deku and the others worldwide on a new mission as they served alongside Endeavor with other major pro-heroes from around the world. It was a big expansion at the time as during Deku and the others' pro-hero internship, they had been thrown into much tougher fights than before. This movie was also one of the first real examples of the kind of global scale we'd see coming in the final war against the villains towards the series' end. Looking back on it now, it really was a bigger tease for the future than fans expected at the time.

My Hero Academia 's TV anime franchise has officially come to an end with its final specials released earlier this Spring, but there's still one major event planned to cap off the 10th anniversary. My Hero Academia Ultra Expo will be taking place on April 17-18 in Japan next year, and it will be gathering members of the production staff and cast as they celebrate how far it's all come in the last ten years. But if we're lucky, we might also see some kind of new anime project announced beyond the end of the TV series.

There have been five My Hero Academia movies released throughout the years, but unfortunately the final season came and went without any new feature film project. These films had been telling original stories taking place in between the anime's big arcs, but there unfortunately wasn't time for one during all of the chaos in the final war. With Deku and the others now adult pro-heroes, it would make a great opportunity for one final movie story.

Are you going to check out My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission on Crunchyroll? Where does it rank among your favorite My Hero Academia movies? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Without This Donkey Kong Game Releasing 32 Years Ago, One Of the Best N64 Platformers Wouldn't Exist
articles.summary: Courtesy of Nintendo The release of Donkey Kong Country was incredibly influential in 1994, marking one of the most iconic SNES games of that era, but its success also allowed developer Rare to keep creating. The trust Nintendo put into Rare ended up paying off in a big way, creating another action platformer for the N64 that once […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The release of Donkey Kong Country was incredibly influential in 1994, marking one of the most iconic SNES games of that era, but its success also allowed developer Rare to keep creating. The trust Nintendo put into Rare ended up paying off in a big way, creating another action platformer for the N64 that once again helped define that era of gaming. In many ways, the existence of Donkey Kong Country set up Rare's next big success, giving players a title that has lived in constant reverence — Banjo-Kazooie .

Banjo-Kazooie released in 1998, continuing Rare's streak of great titles alongside Nintendo, standing up alongside Donkey Kong Country , Killer Instinct , and GoldenEye 007 . The N64 was already a highly regarded home console, with games like 1996's Super Mario 64 taking players by storm with its large world and level design in 3D environments. Banjo-Kazooie took that to a whole new level, establishing the action-platformer sub-genre in a new way that would later inspire other great games like Jak & Daxter , Crash Bandicoot , and Spyro the Dragon for the PlayStation.

The success of Donkey Kong Country for Rare can't be understated, even though the developer was responsible for some great titles before the Mario character's first major spin-off. Rare had come fresh off the arcade-style Battletoads , but despite existing since 1986, the company didn't see a huge hit until the ultra-hard amphibian beat-em-up. Donkey Kong Country was their first attempt at a home console release, and the first time Rare teamed up with Nintendo, the pioneers behind the best home consoles and series tied to them (ever heard of Super Mario Bros. ?).

One of the reasons why Donkey Kong Country was such a huge SNES hit was how it pushed the consoles graphics beyond any other game was capable before. The 3D work in Donkey Kong Country was incredibly good for its time, with presentation and graphic quality helping it reach 9 million copies sold, a huge feat for that time period. The game's details came from a cartoonish charm where fully 3D models and painted environments occupied a lush, tropical environment that was instantly memorable. Although the game's plot was bare bones about Donkey Kong's stolen bananas, the levels were intricate and well designed compared to almost any other platformer.

The game was unrelenting too, with surprising amounts of difficulty you might struggle to find in the genre today. The rail cart sections of Donkey Kong Country are notorious for their aggravating precision requirements, forcing players to have quick timing and a good understanding of the game's physics. Plenty of level secrets and enemy variety made the game enjoyable to replay too, making it a perpetual title in SNES players' households. Without the undeniable appeal Donkey Kong Country had, their collaborations with Nintendo likely couldn't have produced an original IP to rival Nintendo's best.

Rare having the chance to make more games with Nintendo would prove to be a great partnership, helping to establish multiple IPs beyond just Mario, Donkey Kong, or characters in that universe. Killer Instinct was a great original fighting game in arcades, but it wasn't until Banjo-Kazooie that Rare once again made a huge impact on home consoles. The N64 was already a highly popular console, but Banjo-Kazooie 's creativity and expressiveness matched what made Donkey Kong Country great with the same charm. Winning multiple awards in 1998, Banjo-Kazooie is still considered one the best Rare games of all time .

While Super Mario 64 introduced players to the idea of intricate 3D platforming, Banjo-Kazooie is arguably the game that perfected it. The game is once again straightforward, but with much larger levels and tons of collectibles for players to get lost in searching for, making each stage feel dynamic and detailed. Rather than a huge, empty space for players to explore, Rare created themed stages with tons of variety, making areas vibrant or changing as you played. The cartoon style of the game also added a level of comedy into it, with villains like Gruntilda being instantly memorable for rhyming dialogue. Ever since release, players have been charmed by the sounds, music, and hidden Jiggies of the title.

When you think about it, Banjo-Kazooie is almost an evolution of Donkey Kong Country in every way, building on the platforming and charm of the first title to refine the second. Banjo-Kazooie is almost a realization of what Rare was truly capable of, but it wouldn't be possible without their early identity having a chance to grow. There are so many details in Banjo-Kazooie that can almost be considered a step-up from a Donkey Kong Country mechanic, although both games are integral to the history of platformers as a whole.

Do you prefer Banjo-Kazooie or Donkey Kong Country as your favorite Rare IP? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.summary: Not many movies have made a bigger impact on pop culture in 2026 than Obsession. After its initial debut at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025, the movie hit theaters in May 2026 and became a massive hit that is now set to hit Netflix. It grossed more than $500 million on a budget […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Not many movies have made a bigger impact on pop culture in 2026 than Obsession . After its initial debut at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025, the movie hit theaters in May 2026 and became a massive hit that is now set to hit Netflix . It grossed more than $500 million on a budget of less than $1 million, while also receiving widespread acclaim from critics and casual moviegoers. There has even been significant talk of star Inde Navarrette getting nominated for Best Actress at the Academy Awards, which doesn't often happen for stars of horror projects. Obsession has fittingly become something of an obsession for film fans everywhere.

Of course, whenever a movie becomes such a huge success, rumors start to swirl about a sequel. That's especially true when a project is made on such a small budget and ends up dominating at the box office. Studios want more of that kind of profit, meaning Obsession 2 has been brought up several times. Both Inde Navarrette and writer/director Curry Barker have discussed the future of Obsession and each has some unique concepts for what that could feature. Obsession might feel like it works well as a standalone story, but these ideas could open the door for something special.

Inde Navarrette has shot into stardom because of Obsession , evidenced by the Oscars buzz and her landing a coveted role in the MCU's take on the X-Men. Despite her busy schedule, Navarrette said she'd be open to returning for a sequel . She said, "I would totally be open to doing a sequel. Are you kidding me? Who am I to say no? And what is she doing afterwards?" Navarrette would like to see a sequel explore Nikki's grief process after the shocking conclusion of Obsession .

She added, "When things happen that are completely out of our control, like losing a loved one, losing a parent, losing autonomy, having an experience that wasn’t your fault, it’s very difficult to understand anything. She’s just starting the grief process.” While this is an interesting idea, it would be hard to see how the One Wish Willow would play a part since Nikki already used one. The sequel could pick up years later and maybe have Nikki be part of another wish, reigniting her greatest fears.

For those purists who love a film like Obsession and would like to see it remain a standalone project, Curry Barker's idea for what could be next is better for you. He spoke with Deadline about a plot hole in the film, saying that things are far too normal in a world where people use the One Wish Willow. There would be absurd things like dragons around, yet there aren't, so Barker noted, "Every time someone makes a wish, they enter into an alternate reality where their wish comes true, so you’re not experiencing everybody’s wish at the same time."

He admits that the wish about money falling from the ceiling breaks that logic, so there are issues, but the concept is solid. In fact, Barker suggested a sequel concept for an anthology series that would play into that. “Each episode is a different wish that goes completely off the rails. Maybe I’ll direct the pilot with the same DP, and you could invite other filmmakers to kind of give their spin at it. That would be really cool.”

What would you like to see in an Obsession sequel? Tell us your thoughts in the comments section!

articles.content:
Thanksgiving is right around the corner and, of course, many are readying themselves for the festivities that are to come. Of course, Hollywood’s biggest stars will also be prepping for their own holiday activities as well. With that, Brad Pitt was recently asked how he planned to spend Turkey Day this year. The A-lister ultimately provided a brief, but direct, answer to the question. And, most notably, his comment comes amid continued reports about Pitt’s alleged estrangement from his children.

Although the Oscar winner didn’t go into detail, he could’ve been referring to the extended Pitt family. It’s been reported that the Heart of the Beast star maintains close ties with his two younger siblings, Julie Pitt Neal and Doug Pitt. Not only that, but it seems likely that Pitt will also be with his lady, Ines de Ramon, who he’s been dating since 2022. So who’s going to be cooking on the big day, Brad or De Ramon? The actor was asked about that as well, and he shared a funny take:

That kind of answer definitely tracks for Pitt, who usually has no problem making a joke at his own expense. At the same premiere, he also fielded a question about longtime friend and co-star George Clooney, who trolled his dance moves . Pitt clapped back with a funny comment, but also didn’t deny being subpar on the dance floor. As for Thanksgiving, though, it sounds like the F1 star is more than content to let his partner handle the culinary-based obligations.

All the while, if recent reports are to be believed, Brad Pitt isn’t on good terms with the six children he shares with ex-wife Angelina Jolie . Pitt and Jolie are parents to Maddox (25), Pax (22), Zahara (21), Shiloh (20) and twins Knox & Vivienne (18). The last few years have seen several of Pitt’s kids drop his last name and solely maintain their mother’s last name. Simultaneously, Pitt remains engaged in a legal battle with Jolie over the Château Miraval, the winery they formerly co-owned. It’s been alleged that even a decade after Jolie’s initial divorce filing , there are still hard negative feelings between the former couple.

articles.title: 5 of the Best Movie & TV Easter Eggs In GTA 6, Including a Tribute to Paul Walker
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games GTA 6 is part of a series inspired by legendary movies, such as GTA 3 almost being a direct copy of Scarface while The Sopranos, Miami Vice, Heat, No Country for Old Men, and, of course, Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas have been direct inspirations for other GTA games. Even spin-offs like GTA: San Andreas are tied […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google GTA 6 is part of a series inspired by legendary movies, such as GTA 3 almost being a direct copy of Scarface while The Sopranos , Miami Vice , Heat , No Country for Old Men , and, of course, Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas have been direct inspirations for other GTA games. Even spin-offs like GTA: San Andreas are tied to popular media influences, such as Boyz 'n the Hood and other Los Angeles-centered crime dramas. As a result, it's no surprise that GTA 6 has many movie and TV show references, albeit in more direct ways than ever before.

There are plenty of Easter Eggs in GTA 6 already, from hidden cryptids to quests where literal aliens can be found like in past titles from the series. However, players are beginning to point out direct references to specific movies or shows, including a Fast and Furious Easter Egg inspiration that calls back to actor Paul Walker as a fascinating tribute. Considering the gameplay of the GTA series, these references are a great homage to what built the franchise, helping it reach the acclaimed status it has to where everyone wants to take off work to play its latest entry.

The Fast and Furious reference to Paul Walker in GTA 6 comes from the car the actor's character had in the series being something you can get in the game. The green and blue muscle car once owned by Brian O'Conner is called the "Mitsubishi Eclipse" in-game, and is located in a Garage somewhere off the coast of Leonida. Players looking to embody Paul Walker's character in Fast and Furious will have to travel to Vespucci Island to collect the car, but it may be difficult since it isn't connected to a quest you can track. After some searching, you should come across the car naturally to take it for yourself.

While Paul Walker may have driven a Toyota Supra in Furious 7 , the last movie he appeared in before his untimely passing, the 1995 Mitsubishi Eclipse from The Fast and the Furious is a great tribute to the first movie in that high-speed franchise. While you won't be able to drive with Dom in GTA 6 and the rest of his family, the Eclipse is a strong car to own and use during various missions. You may have to steal the car in GTA 6 to acquire it fully, but doing so can help you replicate The Fast and the Furious ' most notorious moments with some nitro boosts of your own.

One of the most subtle movie references in GTA 6 takes place during Chapter 1's final mission, where Lucia has to break Jason out of the hospital after he was hurt. A sudden ambush in the space turns the medical facility into a battleground, where players have to fight through enemy waves to escape. However, this event kicks off with an enemy revealing a shotgun out of a crate of roses, attacking the player in a direct homage to Terminator 2: Judgement Day 's Arnold Schwarzenegger T-800.

In the movie, the T-800 cyborg pulls the same trick, revealing a shotgun while pursuing John Conner, at a time where the movie doesn't reveal that the machine is back from the future to protect him this time. The eerie hallway shot of the older Terminator model crushing a rose with a combat boot is iconic, so it makes complete sense that GTA 6 would pay homage to this legendary scene. However, the enemy with the shotgun in GTA 6 isn't a new protector against the liquid metal T-1000, but rather an enemy you have to put down quickly if you want to survive.

An underrated but incredibly detailed reference in GTA 6 is tied to the TV show Dexter , a show about a serial killer working in a bay area similar to GTA 6 's Leonida. Traveling to the Washington Island sub-area of Vice City will lead you to a series of white apartments, which look fairly conspicuous at first glance. However, going northeast from Penmarch Isle may lead you to the edge of the Trinity Apartments, which Dexter fans will notice are named after The Trinity Killer, a famous antagonist from the show during its fourth season.

Dexter Morgan is a careful, meticulous sort, whose killings are more like personal rituals within an extremely private space rather than something grand and publicized. As a result, when you find an apartment with all its windows shuttered in Trinity Apartments, you'll know you're at the home of shady character. This apartment isn't one you can go into, obviously, but it is a place where a ladder leads to the building's roof, showing where a serial killer keeps their supplies. The Bay Harbor Butcher has clearly been busy, as indicated by two tool boxes, a knife, some gloves, a white rag, and other equipment in this area.

This is a rather detailed reference, as the roof of the GTA 6 apartment is also cluttered with various syringes alongside the tools Dexter Morgan uses. This refers to the way that Dexter knocks out his targets before bringing them back to his "lair" to be killed, which has changed over the seasons of the show. That being said, a boat in the distance visible from the GTA 6 location almost resembles Dexter 's "Slice of Life" ship exactly, mirroring the vehicle Dexter would use to dump bodies of those he'd killed.

While Heat has been an influence on every GTA game, Collateral is another Michael Mann film that is directly replicated in GTA 6 , down to the characters involved in it. At one point in the game, if you are offering taxi services (similar to Jamie Foxx's character Max from the movie), a mysterious stranger might get in the car and pull a gun on you. This is referring to Tom Cruise's character Vincent, a deadly hitman who hires Max to drive to several locations in the dead of night to kill several people tied to the trial of a criminal kingpin. While Vincent isn't violent toward Max right away in the movie, in GTA 6 , it's down to business right away.

The GTA 6 character never says their name, but much like in the movie, they force you to drive them to a specific location, while also telling you to speed past a red light. The calm, matter-of-fact sociopathic behavior of the hitman perfectly reflects the personality of Vincent from Collateral , who remains one of Tom Cruise's most underrated performances . The GTA 6 character is just as calculated as Vincent, as you speeding through a red light is an easy way to get you on traffic cameras, pinning you to his actions. The way this character ropes you into their job is almost a 1:1 to the events of the movie, making it a really fun callback to the 2004 thriller.

The hitman eventually takes you to a secluded alleyway, where some criminals are moving things out of a hideout, including some drugs and money. Much like one of the best scenes in Collateral , you can watch as the hitman quickly fires on and kills the criminals, doing his job with brutal efficiency. This Easter Egg, discovered by X user @Testyment and reposted by DiscussingFilm , ends with the player taking out the hitman using their own skills and looting the hideout. It's unclear what else would happen if you let the hitman go, but it could be assumed that he may try to take you out to cover up loose ends.

There is an actual alien in GTA 6 , along with abductions and strange government research that makes the game look like an episode of The X-Files . That grounded show was filled with sci-fi elements, mixing both the thrilling realism of government conspiracies and criminal activity with questions about the existence of the supernatural. As both Jason and Lucia, you can have some close encounters yourself, with each character going through their own adventures depending on your actions. To find this reference, all you have to do is find a random encounter in Port Gellhorn at night, where a woman is being abducted into the sky by a UFO.

If you're Lucia or Jason, just seeing the UFO will cause you to be abducted next, where you lose consciousness and wake up some time later on the ground. This will unlock the "The Truth is Out There" trophy/achievement, which references the tagline of The X-Files directly. While main characters Mulder and Scully don't appear, you can find similarly entwined characters in the GTA 6 map, with a garage being full of conspiracy theories that look insane at first. Further investigations into the UFO can even lead to Lucia exploring the interior of one, or Jason discovering a secret lab with a real little gray man who desires to return to the stars.

This might be the most detailed Easter Egg in the game, but there are others that go the extra mile to have players interact with them. For example, there are multiple references to Marvel Comics' X-Men through in-game parodies of the mutant team, as well as a quest involving someone acting like The Incredible Hulk. The more you explore GTA 6 , the more references you'll find, making the game feel even larger and packed full of detail than you could have expected.

What has been your favorite Easter Egg to a movie or TV show in GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: 5 DC Superheroes Who Had Their Origin Stories Drastically Changed
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Origin stories are one of the most important elements of establishing a compelling superhero because they help explain their powers, personality, and motivations. However, these origin stories are rarely set in stone, as writers constantly try to modernize or reinvent their characters. DC Comics knows this as well as anyone. The company has rebooted its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Origin stories are one of the most important elements of establishing a compelling superhero because they help explain their powers, personality, and motivations. However, these origin stories are rarely set in stone, as writers constantly try to modernize or reinvent their characters. DC Comics knows this as well as anyone. The company has rebooted its universe several times, reworking practically every hero and villain’s origins. Some of DC’s most iconic superheroes currently have origin stories that are practically unrecognizable from those when they first debuted. These retcons and reboots have ranged from elevating to degrading the mythologies of DC’s greatest heroes.

Every DC character has had their origins rewritten and modernized. Still, these are some of the most extreme examples ever.

Superman arguably has one of the most well-known and straightforward superhero origin stories. Superman was a baby from the planet Krypton who was rocketed to Earth to spare him from his world’s destruction before being adopted by a loving human couple named the Kents. However, Superman’s first appearance in Action Comics #1 differed significantly from his current lore: one example, the Kents didn’t exist. Indeed, in his debut story, when Superman landed on Earth, he was taken in not by farmers, but by an orphanage. This was immediately retconned in Superman #1 the following year , which introduced John and Martha Kent, who adopt the young Kal-El and name him Clark Kent. Another significant part of Superman’s origin that’s been constantly revised is the nature of Krypton’s destruction. The culprits behind Krypton's destruction have ranged from Krypton’s government, Brainiac, the Eradicator, the Black Circle, Rogol Zaar, and General Zod to natural causes. Yet despite these changes to his origin, there has always been one constant—Superman has always remained a paragon of truth and justice.

Wonder Woman’s lineage has long been a hotly debated topic in DC Comics. In her first origin, Diana was sculpted from clay by the Queen of the Amazons, Hippolyta, and given life by Aphrodite. Later writers tried to add a father to the picture. Wonder Woman #152 revealed that Diana was the child of Hippolyta and an unnamed sailor who was lost at sea. And while that origin was immediately scrapped, one reboot with much more staying power came with the New 52 initiative. This reboot revealed that Diana’s creation from clay was a cover story Hippolyta concocted to protect her from Hera’s wrath. Diana was the product of an affair between Zeus and Hippolyta. With the Rebirth initiative undoing many of the changes made during the New 52 era, Wonder Woman’s original backstory was restored, and her familial ties to Zeus were erased. Adding a father to Wonder Woman’s backstory has always devalued how much of a miracle her birth was, so DC finally realized that they had no reason to fix what wasn’t broken.

Today, Aquaman is recognized as the half-human King of Atlantis. However, when Aquaman first debuted during the Golden Age, he was anything but royalty. Arthur Curry’s father was an undersea explorer who, after finding the ruins of Atlantis, found a way to give his son superpowers like breathing underwater, talking to sea life, and super strength. That origin was soon retconned so that Arthur was the son of a human lighthouse keeper and the exiled Queen of Atlantis, Atlanna. With the Crisis on Infinite Earths reboot, DC made Aquaman a full-blooded Atlantean named Orin, adopted by humans who renamed him Arthur Curry. Things got even more complicated when Orin died and his adoptive human cousin, Arthur Joseph Curry, temporarily replaced him, developing his powers from a science experiment. With the New 52 relaunch, DC mercifully returned to Aquaman’s simplest origin: the illegitimate half-breed son of a lighthouse keeper and the Queen of Atlantis, who eventually took his rightful place on the throne.

One of Alan Moore’s greatest achievements as a writer was revealing that everything we thought we knew about Swamp Thing was a lie. When Swamp Thing was introduced, his origin story was that he was a brilliant scientist named Alec Holland, and a lab explosion caused him to merge with the swamp's plant life and become a monster. A huge part of Swamp Thing’s character was the desperate hope that he could be cured and become human again. However, Moore’s critically acclaimed series The Saga of Swamp Thing revealed the awful truth: Alec Holland had died in the explosion. The character we know as Swamp Thing is the product of lab chemicals spilling into the swamp and causing the plants to absorb Alec’s memories. This discovery shattered Swamp Thing’s sense of identity, as he had to accept that he was merely a copy of Holland and was never human. Swamp Thing’s rebooted origin has remained mostly unchanged because of how it challenges concepts of identity and humanity.

No two characters in comic book history have more convoluted, reworked origin stories than Hawkman and Hawkgirl. Originally, they were archaeologists Carter Hall and Shiera Saunders who were reincarnations of Ancient Egyptian lovers who were killed and cursed by an evil priest. After remembering their past lives, Carter and Shiera used material from an alien spacecraft called Nth metal to develop anti-gravity wings. During the 60s, they were rebooted as Kartar and Shiera Hol. These versions were members of the winged Thanagar alien race and were cops who came to Earth to fight crime. From there, Hawkman and Hawkgirl’s origins would be combined, retconned, and rebooted to include things like Hawkgirl being the reincarnation of an angel called Shraa. Meanwhile, Hawkman was temporarily rewritten to be the reincarnation of an alien tyrant called Ktar Deathbringer. Things have gotten so complicated now that there are now two Hawkgirls, Kendra Saunders and Shayera Thal, who are reincarnations of the same person. Hawkman and Hawkgirl are the worst-case scenario of excessive retcons in DC Comics.

Do you think any of these origins are better now than how they once were? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the  ComicBook Forum!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 39 confirms the franchise's new duo, and they might be more compatible than Naruto and Sasuke. Although Naruto and Sasuke are equally strong and have been teammates for a long time, their compatibility has always been one of their biggest issues. With different ambitions and fighting styles, they never truly complemented each other's powers, despite being brothers from distant bloodlines. In fact, across hundreds of episodes, there have only been a handful of instances where they fought together and truly emerged as a duo. Rather, their dynamic has always been that of rivals.

The fight against Momoshiki in the Boruto series was when fans finally got to witness their incredible teamwork. By this point, the two shared the same goals, which is why their dynamic in this fight and later against Isshiki was so exciting to witness. However, with them gone, the question of who would replace them remained. Without any surprises, the series has introduced another Uzumaki and Uchiha duo . Boruto and Sarada's dynamic wasn't clear at the beginning, but the latter admitting her feelings for Boruto and both of them showcasing their resolve to protect each other have shaped them into an epic duo, something the latest chapter of the series highlights perfectly.

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 39 continues to explore Sarada's predicament after being kidnapped by Code and Boruto's arrival to rescue her. The titular protagonist overpowers Code and is ready to leave with Sarada immediately. However, Sarada insists that they have the perfect opportunity to take down Code. Boruto agrees, and the duo comes up with a plan to subdue him. Sarada and Boruto trick Code into thinking that Boruto has folded under pressure. However, Sarada uses her Mangekyo Sharingan ability, Ohirume, to apply gravitational pressure and subdue Code, while Boruto plants both feet on the ground and once again hits Code with Rasengan Uzuhiko, completely defeating him.

This sequence not only highlights the trust Sarada and Boruto have in each other but also shows how well their attacks complement each other. Upon closer examination, both Ohirume and Uzuhiko have elements related to gravity, and the way they use these abilities against Code highlights how even powerful enemies like him wouldn't stand a chance against this deadly combination. However, the main element that arguably makes Sarada and Boruto's duo more compatible than Naruto and Sasuke is their feelings for each other. The Boruto series has been particularly adamant about highlighting the element of love and how it empowers its characters.

Sarada has already showcased this by deliberately allowing Code to kidnap her so that Boruto can execute his plan, demonstrating her trust in him and her willingness to do anything for him. This is something Naruto and Sasuke's duo completely lacked. Whenever the two came together to fight, it wasn't because they cared about each other, especially in Sasuke's case, but rather because of a mutual understanding of their goals. As the prominent Uchiha and Uzumaki of the Naruto sequel, Boruto and Sarada's duo was always going to be highlighted at some point, and the series has now confirmed it through their trust, love, and complementary abilities, which could even help them surpass the iconic duo of Naruto and Sasuke.

However, the money isn’t going to him or Holmes. Instead, it’s going to charity. The details are still a little murky, but we do have more understanding of what went down after the scene in the movie where he brings it up and the card at the end that explains he changed his mind and wasn’t going to profit from the movie. Given how big a box office hit ($89 million and counting) the A24 release has been, it's probably a nice chunk of change. So what is going on? Here’s what we know.

One of the more controversial aspects of the production of You Can See Everything was Evans negotiating a payout with execs from A24 and the movie's co-directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The scene, which sees Evans asking for money after Holmes has left the room, has been a topic of conversation among fans of the film. Even lawyers have chimed in on how it could affect the judgment against Holmes, who owes somewhere north of $400 million in restitution after her conviction on fraud crimes .

In the scene, everyone agrees that Evans (and presumably Holmes) will be paid for their appearances. Then, at the end, a card appears informing the audience that Evans backed off this deal and wouldn’t be paid. Now, a new report in The Hollywood Reporter has clarified it. According to the article, Evans is earning money on the backend, but that money is reportedly going to a children’s charity. The article did not specify which charity.

The outlet also confirmed with A24 that a deal had been struck, but neither the outlet’s sources nor A24 revealed how much the charity would be getting or what percentage of the backend was negotiated. The film is closing in on $100 million at the box office, and it's sure to earn more when it hits VOD sometime in the near future (the exact date is still not confirmed). That’s to say nothing about whatever money the film will earn when it moves to HBO Max, likely in early 2027.

This is yet another saga in a movie that is full of intrigue both on-screen and off. It is also another wrinkle in trying to determine what is true and what is not. That question is at the core of the movie, and it seems even now, weeks after its release and years after Evans and Holmes were filmed before she reported to prison in 2023. That question is still lingering in every aspect. I’ve said before that this movie is like an onion, and this is one more layer getting peeled away, but it’s only offering up another layer that is just as fascinating.

articles.summary: A remake of an exclusive NES RPG is now free for PS5 users with either PlayStation Plus Extra or PlayStation Plus Premium subscription as part of their most recent lineups. How long it's set to be available with these subscriptions, Sony hasn't disclosed. Most commonly, games are added to these tiers in 12-month and 24-month […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A remake of an exclusive NES RPG is now free for PS5 users with either PlayStation Plus Extra or PlayStation Plus Premium subscription as part of their most recent lineups . How long it's set to be available with these subscriptions, Sony hasn't disclosed. Most commonly, games are added to these tiers in 12-month and 24-month chunks. There is no guarantee that is the case here. Whatever the case, it will be plenty of time for subscribers to play the RPG in its entirety.

Back in 1988, in Japan — and then in 1992 in the United States — developer Chunsoft and publisher Enix, before the latter merged with Square Soft to become known as Square Enix, released Dragon Quest III: The Seeds of Salvation . If this name doesn't sound familiar at all, it may be because in the United States the game was known as Dragon Warrior III . In 1996, the game was remade for the SNES, and then remade again in 2001 for the Game Boy Color. More than two decades after this, a third remake was released in 2024 called Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake . It's this remake that has been made free via PS Plus Extra and Plus Premium.

The original game was well received back in 1988. This is most evident by the fact that it was the best-selling game of the late 1980s, at least in Japan. In the United States, its footprint was smaller, just like the series as a whole. While it didn't sell as well as it did in Japan, it did receive a warm reception among Western consumers. And the same is true of Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake , which hit an 84 on Metacritic . Meanwhile, it has a similar user review score on the PlayStation Store. To this end, it has a 4.24 out of 5 stars on the digital PlayStation Store, which is roughly an 85 on a 100-point scale.

A Classic RPG Reborn With a New Look Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake is specifically a remake of the classic RPG done in the art style of Octopath Traveler , another Square Enix RPG series that debuted in 2018. And if you know your RPGs, you will know Octopath Traveler's primary claim to fame is its beautiful art style, which combines 2D traditional RPG art with a modern 3D presentation.

Dragon Quest III is a self-contained and isolated story. It's not connected to its previous two games, which it actually serves as a prequel to in terms of timeline. As for the game's story, it puts you into the shoes of the 16-year-old son of Ortega, a great hero who previously left his wife and child behind on a quest to defeat the villainous Archfiend, Baramos, but failed. Baramos still threatens the world, and now the king of Aliahan has summoned you to do what your father couldn't.

Those who end up checking out the Square Enix RPG now that it is free with two of the three tiers of PlayStation Plus should expect to sink 30 to 35 hours into the game just to mainline it. Add side content, and this range is more like 40 to 45 hours. Meanwhile, completionists will need to put more like 65 to 70 hours into the old-school RPG.
